project.name: NurCLI
project.tagline: 65 provider routes, 52 tools and 114 Jev engines in one Rust agent

nodes.label: CLI / TUI / headless
nodes.detail: Command parsing, session bootstrap, Gold TUI streaming, and `nur run` all converge on the same runner; UI events carry text, reasoning, tools, approvals, and usage.

nodes.label: AgentRunner
nodes.detail: Owns user turns, model rounds, truncation continuation, compaction, tool-call cycles, delegated work, usage emission, receipts, and state checkpoints.

nodes.label: Subagent runner
nodes.detail: Runs focused delegated prompts with provider/model overrides, admission control, bounded recursion, shared cancellation, coordinated events, and reduced tools.

nodes.label: Fusion panel
nodes.detail: Fans one task across configured model routes in parallel, labels each panel response, and returns evidence for a synthesizing model round.

nodes.label: PromptContext
nodes.detail: Assembles the system prompt once per user turn, then re-renders live permission mode, todo state, workspace identity, environment, and runtime policy each round.

nodes.label: Context controller
nodes.detail: Prunes superseded tool observations, promotes saved context variables, estimates the active window, and compacts transcripts while preserving durable state.

nodes.label: ResponseRequest
nodes.detail: Combines model id, transcript items, instructions, tools, reasoning effort, cache key, media, and output reserve into one protocol-neutral request.

nodes.label: Failover controller
nodes.detail: Retries transient failures and configured fallback routes only before visible output streams, preserving idempotency and preventing duplicate transcript text.

nodes.label: ApiClient
nodes.detail: Applies route selection, OAuth context, retries, idempotency, media normalization, telemetry, and dispatch into one of four wire protocols.

nodes.label: Provider catalog
nodes.detail: Defines every route's id, display name, endpoint, default model, protocol style, credential source, OAuth capability, and model normalization behavior.

nodes.label: Credential routing
nodes.detail: Builds provider-specific authorization, supports subscription and CLI-backed sessions, and refreshes eligible OAuth credentials after unauthorized responses.

nodes.label: Responses adapter
nodes.detail: Serializes Responses-style input and tools, records attempts, handles retryable HTTP failures, and normalizes JSON or server-sent events.

nodes.label: Permission + ToolHost
nodes.detail: Approval classes, read-only parallel batches and deny/ask rules; core tool schemas first, the full surface later, including dogwood policy checks and the diagram plane.

nodes.label: Headroom pipeline
nodes.detail: Registers successful tool bodies, rejects secret-shaped preservation, compresses observations for the model window, and spills oversized results to durable blobs.

nodes.label: Durable runtime state
nodes.detail: Atomically stores transcript sessions, cwd links, context blobs, and vector/graph/hierarchical memory residents under ~/.nur, with backups and scoped recall.

nodes.label: Usage + receipt ledgers
nodes.detail: Every primary, retry, failover and Jev call recorded with its served route; a private local usage ledger aggregates spend without uploading keys.

nodes.label: Direct model labs / 16
nodes.detail: Meta, OpenAI, OpenAI Chat, Anthropic, Google, Antigravity, xAI, DeepSeek, Mistral, Cohere, AI21, Reka, Inception, Writer, Upstage, Thinking Machines, Poolside.

nodes.label: Cloud + SSO / 5
nodes.detail: Hugging Face, Azure OpenAI, and Amazon Bedrock.

nodes.label: Asian model labs / 7
nodes.detail: Kimi Code, Moonshot, Z.AI, Alibaba Qwen, MiniMax, StepFun, and Baichuan.

nodes.label: Local servers / 5
nodes.detail: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, and Jan.

nodes.label: Protocol adapters
nodes.detail: Anthropic Messages, Gemini Cloud Code, and Chat Completions for every non-Responses provider.

nodes.label: TypeSafe / Jev layer
nodes.detail: Batched typed decisions in the loop: which calls still earn their tokens, whether a result worked, what compaction drops, which model fits. Any System One engine plugs in.

nodes.label: Jev engine gateway
nodes.detail: One System One HTTP contract over local Python adapters and source runtimes, with per-engine credentials and owned bridge lifecycle.

nodes.label: OptMem + Connectome
nodes.detail: Permanent OptMem memory outside sessions plus Connectome's self-authored hierarchy, chronicle and checkpoints, scoped per project.

nodes.label: Jev library / 114
nodes.detail: Pinned JevBench v1.5.4 roster plus reviewed newer releases: interface, source, license and connection steps per engine; keys isolated per engine.

nodes.label: Enclave security agents
nodes.detail: Pentests, code security review and findings over Enclave's MCP server, spoken natively; every call is approval-gated and high impact.

nodes.label: GPT-6 Astra
nodes.detail: OpenAI's most capable model (1.05M context). The Ultrafast tier streams up to 6x faster in the API (gpt-6-astra-ultrafast).

nodes.label: GPT-6.1 Sol
nodes.detail: Near-Astra coding and computer use at a fifth of the price (DevDay, Sep 29). nur's default OpenAI model, effort low to max over Responses.

nodes.label: GPT-6 Luna
nodes.detail: OpenAI's efficient tier for focused, high-volume work; also listed as a Jev-class judge in the JevBench roster.

nodes.label: Claude Fable 5.1
nodes.detail: Anthropic's model for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work (Sep 1), adaptive thinking, 1M context.

nodes.label: Claude Opus 5.5
nodes.detail: Anthropic's recommended starting model (Sep 22) for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
nodes.detail: Faster, cheaper complement to Opus 5.5 (Sep 28); nur's default Anthropic model over the Messages API.

nodes.label: Gemini 4 Argon
nodes.detail: First Gemini 4 model (Sep 30): #1 in Text Arena with a 1M-token output limit, rolling out through Google's Fairwind program first.

nodes.label: Gemini 3.8 Flash
nodes.detail: Google's latest stable model for long-horizon engineering and agents (Sep 2); nur's default Gemini route.

nodes.label: Gemini 3.1 Pro
nodes.detail: Google's current Pro tier for advanced problem solving, in preview on the Gemini API.

nodes.label: Grok 4.7
nodes.detail: SpaceXAI's strongest coding and knowledge-work model (Sep 21), about 2.1T parameters; nur's default xAI id.

nodes.label: Muse Spark 1.3
nodes.detail: Meta's agentic multimodal model for longer tool-based work (Sep 2), 1M context; nur's default Meta route.

nodes.label: DeepSeek V4-Pro-0813
nodes.detail: DeepSeek's open-weight flagship (Aug 13); deepseek-flash serves V4.1-Flash (MIT, Sep 10).

nodes.label: Mistral Medium 3.5
nodes.detail: Mistral's frontier multimodal model for agentic and coding work (v26.04).

nodes.label: Command A+
nodes.detail: Cohere's Apache-2.0 218B MoE for enterprise and sovereign deployments.

nodes.label: Laguna S 2.1
nodes.detail: Poolside's open-weight agentic coding model: 8B active, 1M context.

nodes.label: Inkling
nodes.detail: Thinking Machines' Apache-2.0 975B MoE (41B active) with a thinking-effort dial.

nodes.label: Mercury 2.5
nodes.detail: Inception's diffusion language model (Sep 8): parallel decoding at very high token rates.

nodes.label: Solar Mini 4
nodes.detail: Upstage's newest compact model (Sep 23) alongside Solar Pro 3.

nodes.label: Palmyra X6
nodes.detail: Writer's flagship (Aug 13) for long unattended agent work at $2/$8 per MTok.

nodes.label: Reka Edge
nodes.detail: Reka's efficient 7B vision-language model, with Flash and Core for general work.

nodes.label: Kimi K3
nodes.detail: Moonshot's 2.8T open-weight model (Jul 16) with always-on thinking and 1M context; nur's default Moonshot id.

nodes.label: Qwen3.8 Max Prime
nodes.detail: Alibaba's current flagship tier (Sep 23). Qwen 4 was previewed at Apsara on Sep 22 and has no release yet.

nodes.label: GLM-5.3 Prime
nodes.detail: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 line: Prime (Sep 23) and FlashX (MIT, Sep 18); glm-5.3 is nur's default Z.ai model.

nodes.label: MiniMax M3
nodes.detail: MiniMax's open-weight multimodal MoE with 1M context; M3.1-Flash-Preview (Sep 27) runs inside MiniMax Code only.

nodes.label: Step 5 Preview
nodes.detail: StepFun's 600B MoE (27B active) for long-horizon agents (Sep 20); open weights are scheduled for Oct 15.

nodes.label: Amazon Nova 2 Pro
nodes.detail: Amazon's Nova 2 reasoning models on Bedrock with three thinking intensities.

nodes.label: Nemotron 3 Ultra
nodes.detail: NVIDIA's 550B open MoE (Jun) and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (Aug), served through NIM and inference clouds.

nodes.label: Jev 1.13
nodes.detail: TypeSafe's System One decision model (Sep 15) and nur's default judge for tool gating, result checks, compaction and routing.

nodes.label: GLiDE
nodes.detail: Fastino's thinking decision model (Sep 30) on a System One-compatible API: nur jev use --engine glide.

nodes.label: Perplexity Decider 27B
nodes.detail: Perplexity's open decision model (Oct 1): typed choice, yes/no and score answers, listed in nur's Jev library.

nodes.label: Cygnet
nodes.detail: Top-ranked open engine on JevBench v1.5.4, one of 114 entries in nur's Jev library.
